history.title: Army of Bombay → Bombay: failure; 0 officer losses.
history.report:
13 dice after 1 defence. Committed: 12 regiments, 2 officers; alliances: none.

Exhaust 12 regiments, 2 officers and 0 local alliances. Return 0 lost officers to their players’ supplies. Never remove regiments for this loss check.

Region control, orders, unrest and Elephant position stay as they were.

lines.text: The expedition had been undertaken with every expectation of success. The Company's expectations, unfortunately, had not been consulted by the enemy.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: The expedition has failed to change the position in Bombay. We shall not mistake that for a permanent settlement.
lines.speaker: Narayan of Bombay

lines.text: “I should hesitate to call this a defeat. Several important objectives were achieved, including the discovery of objectives that we ought not to have attempted.”
lines.speaker: Thomas Reed

history.title: Army of Bombay → Bombay: success; 0 officer losses.
history.report:
13 dice after 1 defence. Committed: 12 regiments, 2 officers; alliances: none.

Exhaust 12 regiments, 2 officers and 0 local alliances. Return 0 lost officers to their players’ supplies. Never remove regiments for this loss check.

Distribute £8 loot: Commander £1 plus £1 per own surviving officer, then clockwise £1 per surviving officer. Pay the bank £1 per regiment and alliance. Repeat while cash remains; stop when it runs out.

Take 1 trophies; remove the target’s tower and dome. Open all its orders and remove all its unrest.

Move Bombay’s loot/control token, region side faceup, above the Bombay President. Place its Governor overlay and put its Governor card in Vacant Offices.

lines.text: The Company had taken possession of the territory. Explaining why this was necessary would occupy considerably more time than the conquest itself.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: “The Company believes this matter concluded. I admire its confidence.”
lines.speaker: Narayan of Bombay

lines.text: “An excellent victory. I recommend informing London immediately, preferably before anyone begins asking what the expedition cost.”
lines.speaker: Thomas Reed

history.title: Bombay · Tax 1 this turn
history.report:
Resolve the successful Tax’s £2 payment on the table.

First Tax in Bombay this turn: add no unrest. Later Taxes in this region add one unrest each.

lines.text: “Your directors are welcome to my treasury. I only ask that they leave enough for me to purchase it back.”
lines.speaker: Narayan of Bombay

lines.text: “A most encouraging result. The natives have demonstrated a remarkable willingness to contribute to their own improvement.”
lines.speaker: Thomas Avery

history.title: Bombay · Tax 2 this turn
history.report:
Resolve the successful Tax’s £2 payment on the table.

Add 1 unrest to Bombay (now 1).

lines.text: The Company had expected gratitude, or at least obedience. The inhabitants, demonstrating their usual difficulty with administrative terminology, appeared to have confused both with resentment.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: “A discontented population is a dangerous thing. Particularly when those responsible for its discontent believe themselves universally adored.”
lines.speaker: Narayan of Bombay

lines.text: The Tax has been recorded. The payment remains a matter for the physical table.
lines.speaker: Thomas Avery

history.title: Army of Bombay → Bombay: catastrophic failure; 1 officer losses.
history.report:
14 dice after 0 defence. Committed: 12 regiments, 2 officers; alliances: none.

Exhaust 12 regiments, 2 officers and 0 local alliances. Return 1 lost officers to their players’ supplies. Never remove regiments for this loss check.

First return half the Commander’s trophies, rounded up, to supply. Return the Commander to their player’s supply. Flip the office card into Vacant Offices and return its fatigue. This office takes no further actions this turn.

Region control, orders, unrest and Elephant position stay as they were.

lines.text: The expedition had ended disastrously. Its architects were already preparing explanations, an undertaking for which they appeared considerably better equipped.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: The expedition has failed to change the position in Bombay. We shall not mistake that for a permanent settlement.
lines.speaker: Narayan of Bombay

lines.text: “It is essential that London understands the true nature of this affair. I recommend that we describe it as an unexpectedly comprehensive reconnaissance.”
lines.speaker: Thomas Reed
